topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture around cancer hallmarks and explains how they will be connected to mutations and tissue changes.

topics.label: Signaling mutations that deregulate growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways free cancer cells from normal growth control.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted cell maturation contributes to cancer using hematological and intestinal examples.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how mutations alter the balance controlling mitochondrial apoptosis so that cancer cells survive.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and tumor cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the telomere-dependent limit on cell division and how cancer cells overcome it through increased telomerase expression.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and the growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the treatment of mutation-driven growth control by explaining p53's protective stress responses and recapping the hallmarks discussed.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and feeds back into its molecular regulation.

topics.label: Angiogenesis supporting tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the angiogenic switch supplies the vascular support needed for tumors to grow.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and successful secondary tumor formation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells spread to distant sites and what determines whether that spread produces detectable metastases.

topics.label: Closing summary and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture's central message about shared hallmarks, recommends further reading, and invites questions.
